speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel the pain in your wrist and when it started, and tell me if you have any difficulty moving your hand.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis. The patient's history of thumb/wrist pain radiating to the elbow, worsening with infant holding, and a specific fall six months ago is highly suggestive of this condition. I will order a wrist ultrasound to confirm tendon inflammation and rule out a distal radius fracture from her fall. REQUEST TEST: Wrist_Ultrasound.
